# Cross-Branch Linkages & Internal References

This page outlines neurochemical, physiological, and behavioral connections between modules of the companion. By linking botanical kinetics to cortical activation, and physical somatosensory priming to game-theoretic outcomes, the matrix below establishes a unified multi-disciplinary framework. Eleven high-value linkages from the Cross-Branch Linkages pack:

| Source Branch → Target Branch | Scientific Rationale & Primary Citations |
| --- | --- |
| 1.4 Active Compound Profiles (L-Theanine Tmax) ↓ 2.2 Neural Wave Signatures (Resting Alpha onset) | Oral L-theanine reaches peak plasma concentration (Tmax) between 35–50 minutes post-ingestion, directly predicting the 30–45 minute physiological delay observed before significant relative alpha-band (8–12 Hz) power increases manifest on an EEG. Citations: van der Pijl et al. (2010); Nobre et al. (2008); Scheid et al. (2012). |
| 3.3 Embodied Cognition (Thermal Priming) ↓ 4.3 Game-Theoretic Interactions (Trust Game payoffs) | Holding a warm (60°C) beverage cup activates the anterior insular cortex, which physically primes social cognition and increases first-mover trust allocations in the Trust Game by +24.8%. Citations: Williams & Bargh (2008); Kang et al. (2011); Inagaki & Eisenberger (2013). |
| 1.3 Extraction Kinetics (Temperature thresholds) ↓ 1.4 Active Compound Profiles (EGCG ratios) | Extraction of EGCG is highly temperature-dependent due to its high diffusion activation energy (Ea ≈ 30 kJ/mol), meaning brewing green tea below 80°C significantly lowers the EGCG-to-Caffeine ratio, reducing cellular signaling yield. Citations: Spiro & Siddique (1981); Perva-Uzunalić et al. (2006); Del Rio et al. (2004). |
| 2.3 Endocrinological Response (HPA Axis cortisol) ↓ 4.2 Risk Propensity (Loss Aversion λ) | Stress-induced HPA-axis activation spikes systemic cortisol levels, which acts as a neurochemical moderator that reduces the loss aversion coefficient (λ ≈ 1.62) and increases risky financial behavior under pressure. Citations: Coates & Herbert (2008); Yoto et al. (2012); Rogers et al. (2013). |
| 3.4 Ritual Psychology (Scripted task predictability) ↓ 2.4 Physiological Biomarkers (Autonomic HRV buffering) | Executing a highly structured, invariant tea-brewing sequence provides top-down cognitive predictability that lowers sympathetic arousal, as evidenced by a 15.4 ms increase in RMSSD (vagal HRV). Citations: Brooks et al. (2016); Lang et al. (2015); Kimura et al. (2007). |
| 2.1 Synaptic Mechanisms (Glutamate antagonism) ↓ 4.1 Dual-Process Dynamics (System 2 task accuracy) | L-theanine acts as a low-affinity competitive antagonist at ionotropic glutamate receptors, mitigating sensory distractibility and sustaining analytical System 2 attention during continuous task-switching batteries. Citations: Kakuda (2011); Gomez-Ramirez et al. (2007); Haskell et al. (2008). |
| 2.2 Neural Wave Signatures (Beta-wave up-regulation) ↓ 2.4 Physiological Biomarkers (Autonomic SCR spike) | Unmitigated caffeine-induced adenosine antagonism drives high-frequency cortical beta oscillations (12–30 Hz), which strongly correlate with elevated peripheral sympathetic arousal, manifested as spiked skin conductance levels (+0.88 μS). Citations: Barry et al. (2005); Dawson et al. (2007); Rogers et al. (2008). |
| 3.2 Spiritual & Micro-History (Eisai's heart-nourishing theory) ↓ 2.4 Physiological Biomarkers (Vagal RMSSD activation) | Eisai's 1211 AD pharmaceutical claim that tea's bitter flavor (ku) "nourishes the heart" aligns with modern clinical findings showing that tea's active compounds increase parasympathetic vagal tone and RMSSD intervals. Citations: Eisai (1211); Sen (1998); Kimura et al. (2007). |
| 2.1 Synaptic Mechanisms (GABAA positive modulation) ↓ 4.2 Risk Propensity (Present-bias discounting β) | Ethanol's positive allosteric modulation of post-synaptic GABAA receptors slows prefrontal cortex firing, triggering extreme present-bias (temporal discounting β → 0) and rendering subjects blind to future liabilities. Citations: Mihic et al. (1997); Reynolds et al. (2006); George et al. (2005). |
| 3.4 Ritual Psychology (Anxiety buffering) ↓ 4.3 Game-Theoretic Interactions (Ultimatum Game rejection) | Repetitive ritual scripting blunts the neurophysiological error alarm amplitude (ERN) in the anterior cingulate cortex, lowering somatic anxiety and preventing the hyper-aggressive rejection of unequal offers (≤ 30%) in bargaining games. Citations: Hobson et al. (2017); Brooks et al. (2016); Morewedge et al. (2014). |
| 1.1 Species Genetics (var. assamica baseline) ↓ 1.2 Oxidation Kinetics (Thearubigin yield) | The elevated concentration of total catechins (25%–35% dry weight) in var. assamica leaves provides a dense substrate for PPO dimerization, resulting in significantly higher yields of thearubigins during rolling. Citations: Borchetia et al. (2009); Tanaka & Kouno (2003); Lakenbrink et al. (2000). |
